title: HAZEM RADHOUANI
description: Architect with international experience: project work in Tunisia, France and Morocco, and research experience in Japan.
$reel: D104/D120. layout: trio (main left, side top right, drawing bottom right), trio-m (mirrored), duo-p (portrait main 4:5 plus drawing), film (trio with the scrub film as main), duo (two renders; Hay Mohammadi has no drawing). Renders (main, side) are cropped 16:10 by object-fit at pos; drawings are cutouts in images/cut, whole on a sheet card, never cropped. why = the reason for the choice (not published).

reel.why: The case-study hero (day, platform) against the lit station at dusk; the access axonometric shows the hall bridging the tracks.
Portrait hero, so duo-p; the raised and lowered volumes are the project's strategy in one drawing.
Three scales: the site from the air, a shaded courtyard at eye level, the wall and timber shade structure as a detail.
Night section against the daytime aerial; the passenger-flow axonometric reads at card size (the exploded structure was too faint).
Street and courtyard, the project's only two renders; the brick west facade drawn beside the brick render.
Portrait hero, so duo-p; a PRO/DCE project, so its constructive facade-module axonometric is the drawing.
The existing scrub film (D96) as main; the figures at the window give the pavilion's scale; the roof elevation's hatch reads at card size.
Portrait hero, so duo-p; the cross-section's black cut shows the floors at card size.
Outside and inside; a formal-research volume, the bold one of the series at card size.
The screen facade close and the hall across the tracks; the ground-floor plan reads at card size (the structural concept was too faint).
A 16:10 crop would cut the top of the building, so a 4:5 portrait crop (duo-p); the south elevation is the face the render shows.
The red foyer and the facade at dusk; the sketch of the ideas beside them.
No drawing in the content, so two renders: the aerial as main (the 2.85:1 front loses its ends at 16:10), the front cropped to keep the station's sign.
Pool side and front; the plans read at card size (the site plan was too faint).
The path between the wings at eye level and the campus from the air; the site plan places the wings.
